subject: BlueCove: comparative inference evaluation & SLO test plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver King <oliver@bluecove.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@bluecove.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: BlueCove: comparative inference evaluation & SLO test plan

Hi Oliver / Maya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned while you evaluate Redwood vs the hyperscaler and the other APIs you mentioned. High-level asks we captured:

- Primary concerns: consistent p99 latency under burst, transparent per-tenant error budgets, and graceful failover across regions.
- Benchmarks you want: 99th/95th/median latency across 256/1024 token traces, steady-state throughput at 60 qps, and cold-start/failover behavior under network partition.
- Non-functional: rate limits that support spikes without excessive throttling, predictable billing under batching, and audit logs for compliance.

Attached is a short Redwood summary (redwood-performance-summary.pdf) highlighting our runtime optimizations and quantization options. Proposed test matrix:

1) Baseline throughput & latency (256 / 1024 tokens; 10k requests each) — compare Redwood hosted, Redwood-Dedicated (single-pod), and Hyperscaler-A managed endpoint.
2) Rate-limit ramp: step from 10 qps to 200 qps across 5 minutes; measure 429s and queuing latency.
3) Failover probe: inject region outage, validate automatic fallback to secondary region and cold-cache penalty.
4) Error-budget stress: inject intermittent 5% error for 30m and observe degradation / retry behavior.

Can you confirm these are the right axes and whether you want any additional tests (e.g., KV-cache hit-rate experiments or batching sensitivity)? If this looks good I’ll assign owners on our side and propose specific test dates next week.

Next steps I propose:
- Oliver/Maya: confirm test axes and any gaps by EOD Monday.
- Redwood: share executable test scripts and test data, propose run windows.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m retrospective call after the first run to review results.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-performance-summary.pdf
From: Oliver King <oliver@bluecove.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@bluecove.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueCove: comparative inference evaluation & SLO test plan

Rishi —

Thanks for the concise plan, this covers most of it. Two clarifications from our side:

1) For failover we need to validate not only region failover but also fallback from Managed to Dedicated (we run a hybrid in prod). Can Redwood simulate a capacity-constrained Dedicated pool and surface the routing decision timeline?
2) On rate limiting: we want an SLO-style spec: 99.9% of requests should see <150ms queuing overhead before hitting the model under normal load; under spike we want graceful shedding with clear 429 behavior and documented retry-after. We’ll attach our current SLO doc so you can match metrics.

Attaching BlueCove current SLOs for reference (bluecove-current-slo.pdf). Also, would appreciate the exact test harness you intend to run so we can mirror our internal telemetry.

We’re targeting a decision window by the end of the month, so getting test results early next week would be ideal.

O.

Attachments: bluecove-current-slo.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver King <oliver@bluecove.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@bluecove.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueCove: comparative inference evaluation & SLO test plan

Oliver — great, thanks for the SLO doc. We can cover both the region failover and the Managed->Dedicated routing scenario. Action items below and I’ve attached the test scripts we’ll use (slo-test-scripts.sh) so your infra team can vet them.

Owner assignments (proposed):
- Baseline throughput & latency: Monica (monica_patel) — will run hosted vs dedicated vs hyperscaler-A comparisons.
- Rate-limit ramp & error-budget stress: Neha (neha_kapoor) — will capture 429 rates and retry behavior with detailed telemetry.
- Failover / routing timeline: Priyom (priyom_das) — will coordinate capacity constraints and simulated region outage.

Test windows we propose:
- Canary run: Monday 10/25, 10:00–12:00 PT (short runs to validate harness).
- Full run: Tuesday 10/26, 01:00–05:00 PT (longer, includes error-budget stress).

Please confirm: 10/25 canary and 10/26 full run. If you need a different timezone slot we can shift.

Attachments: slo-test-scripts.sh, bluecove-ma-compare.xlsx (empty template for result capture)

Rishi
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueCove: comparative inference evaluation & SLO test plan

All —

Can confirm owners and a few technical notes to ensure the data is actionable:

- For latency traces use real token distributions: 70% short (<=128 tokens), 25% mid (129–512), 5% long (513–1k). This will show the effect of KV cache and attention scaling.
- When we simulate Dedicated capacity constraint, we’ll cap GPU slots rather than kill nodes — this gives realistic queueing vs full failover. Priyom will set a scheduler flag to force routing to fallback after queued wait >3s.
- For 429s: we’ll return Retry-After in seconds and log both client-side and server-side timestamps to compute queuing overhead.
- Error-budget stress: introduce 5% randomized transient 500s across model hosts for 30 minutes; measure downstream retry jitter and successful p99 latency.

I’ll prepare the telemetry dashboard (tokens/billing estimate, p50/p95/p99, 429 rate, retry delay histogram) and share the Drive link before the canary.

Neha
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueCove: comparative inference evaluation & SLO test plan

Quick update on orchestration —

- Canary confirmed: Mon 10/25 10:00–11:30 PT (we’ll keep it shorter than originally proposed). Full run moved to Tue 10/26 00:30–04:30 PT to hit low‑traffic window for BlueCove.
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedDrive — has harness logs and the initial results template (bluecove-ma-compare.xlsx).
- HubSpot: I’ve created a deal task and linked the run in HubSpot deal BC-2026-1437 for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/BC-2026-1437

Notes for engineering: when we run the Managed->Dedicated fallback, we will simulate network egress latency increase to the Managed region then force routing policy change to Dedicated. This reproduces the tail latency spike we discussed.

Priyom
Engineering Lead, Inference Orchestration

From: Oliver King <oliver@bluecove.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@bluecove.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueCove: comparative inference evaluation & SLO test plan

Rishi —

Appreciate the detail and the quick turnaround from your team. Canary slot is confirmed for 10/25 10:00 PT; we’ll have two telemetry engineers observing from our side.

Two asks before the canary:
- Please surface per-request route metadata in logs (region, pool-type, model-variant) so we can independently validate routing decisions.
- During the failover probe please include a short canary where we intentionally send a small mix of high-cache-hit and low-cache-hit prompts to measure cold-cache penalty.

We’ll plan to review the canary results in a 30m sync the same day. If all good, we’ll move to the full run and aim for a procurement decision by 10/31.

Oliver
Director of Platform Engineering, BlueCove Analytics
